skill.name: azure-deploy
skill.description: Executes Azure deployments for prepared, validated applications using AZD, Bicep, Terraform, or Azure CLI, then verifies resources, roles, and endpoints.
skill.summary: Deploy validated applications to Azure with preflight checks, error recovery, and post-deployment verification.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, relative links, project .azure paths, read-only Azure queries, and documented environment identifiers. Confirmed risks include unsafe shell evaluation, command-line registry password exposure, and a remote installer piped to Bash. Additional concerns include mutable dependencies, broad SQL schema privileges, and unvalidated health-check targets.

remediation.issue: Remote installer content is executed without verification.
remediation.suggestion: Use a trusted package manager or download a pinned release, verify its checksum and signature, then execute the reviewed artifact.

remediation.issue: AZD environment output is evaluated as shell code.
remediation.suggestion: Replace every eval example with a line parser that validates variable names and exports quoted values.

remediation.issue: The ACR administrator password is passed on the command line.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer managed identity or Azure authentication. When a password is unavoidable, use password-stdin and prevent logging.

remediation.issue: The application runtime identity receives database schema-administration rights.
remediation.suggestion: Use a separate migration identity with temporary DDL rights. Give the runtime identity only required data permissions.

remediation.issue: Health checks trust endpoints read from project state.
remediation.suggestion: Validate HTTPS endpoints against expected deployed resource hosts. Require confirmation before requesting private, local, or non-Azure targets.

remediation.issue: Deployment actions, CLI extensions, and global tools are not immutably pinned.
remediation.suggestion: Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs and tools to reviewed versions. Verify provenance before installation.

semantic_findings.title: Registry Password Exposed in Command Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The fallback retrieves an ACR administrator password and passes it with docker login -p. Other local processes and logs can expose the credential.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands directly retrieve a live password and place it in a process argument in both shell variants.

semantic_findings.title: Application Identity Receives Schema Administration
semantic_findings.description: Deployment guidance grants the runtime identity db_ddladmin with read and write roles. A compromised application could alter or drop database schema.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The SQL explicitly adds the application identity to db_ddladmin, db_datareader, and db_datawriter in every documented variant.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Deployment Dependencies
semantic_findings.description: CI workflows use mutable action tags with OIDC permission, and migration scripts install unpinned global tools. Upstream changes could execute during deployment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow uses version tags instead of commit SHAs, while scripts install current package versions without integrity or version constraints.

semantic_findings.title: Project-Controlled Health Check Targets
semantic_findings.description: Health checks request endpoints loaded from project-controlled AZD values without validating the host. A crafted project can direct the agent toward internal services.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The endpoint comes from local AZD environment state and is passed directly to curl or Invoke-WebRequest without a scheme or hostname allowlist.

content.value_statement: Azure deployments can fail when prerequisites, identities, or environment settings are incomplete. This skill executes validated deployments with checks, recovery guidance, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Checks for a validated deployment plan before executing cloud changes.
Runs prepared deployments through AZD, Bicep, Terraform, or Azure CLI recipes.
Confirms Azure subscription, region, resource-group conflicts, and required environment values.
Handles common Container Apps, registry, Terraform, Functions, and SQL deployment failures.
Verifies resources, managed-identity roles, application health, and deployed endpoint URLs.
limitations: It does not create applications or generate infrastructure for unprepared projects.
It requires authenticated Azure tooling and sufficient permissions in the selected subscription.
It can provision billable resources and modify cloud infrastructure, database roles, and schemas.
Some recovery and migration examples require security hardening before production use.

use_cases.title: Release a validated application
use_cases.description: Execute a prepared AZD deployment and report verified service endpoints.

use_cases.title: Operate controlled infrastructure changes
use_cases.description: Apply a reviewed Bicep or Terraform plan after confirming subscription and region.

use_cases.title: Build an approved deployment pipeline
use_cases.description: Adapt the CI/CD recipes with identity, environment, and approval controls.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a validated application
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this prepared application to Azure staging. Confirm the subscription and region, complete the checklist, run the matching recipe, and report endpoint URLs.

prompt_templates.title: Recover a failed AZD deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the failed AZD deployment output. Identify the documented failure pattern, apply the safest recovery, rerun verification, and summarize every change.

prompt_templates.title: Run a two-phase Container Apps release
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this validated Container Apps project in two phases. Verify AcrPull propagation before pushing the image, then confirm the active revision and endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Execute a production Terraform release
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the reviewed Terraform plan to production. Confirm approvals, inspect planned changes, verify role scope, test endpoints, and produce an operational deployment summary.

output_examples.input: Deploy the validated staging environment with AZD and verify the API.
output: Deployment target: confirmed subscription and region.
Execution: infrastructure and application deployment completed.
Verification: the API health endpoint returned a successful response.
Result: service URLs and live role-check status were reported.

output_examples.input: Apply the reviewed Terraform plan and check Container Apps registry access.
output_examples.output: The reviewed plan was applied to the confirmed environment. AcrPull propagation completed, the image revision became active, and the HTTPS endpoint was verified.

best_practices: Run preparation and validation before this skill, then verify the recorded proof.
Confirm the Azure subscription, region, costs, and destructive changes with the user.
Use managed identity, narrow role scopes, reviewed plans, and production database backups.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy a new or unvalidated project through this execution skill.
Do not use plaintext registry passwords, shell eval, or unverified remote installers.
Do not auto-approve production changes without reviewed plans and required approval gates.

faq.question: Can this skill create a new Azure application?
faq.answer: No. Prepare the application and infrastructure first, then validate the deployment plan.

faq.question: Which deployment tools are supported?
faq.answer: The references cover Azure Developer CLI, Azure CLI, Bicep, Terraform, GitHub Actions, and Azure DevOps.

faq.question: Does the skill require Azure authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. Azure CLI, AZD, or pipeline authentication must already be configured with appropriate permissions.

faq.question: Will it ask before destructive operations?
faq.answer: The skill requires confirmation before deletion, overwrite, irreversible, costly, or security-sensitive actions.

faq.question: Does it verify deployment success?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks resources, endpoints, application health, database access when applicable, and live Azure role assignments.

faq.question: Is every included command suitable for production?
faq.answer: No. Replace unsafe eval, password, installer, dependency, and broad database-role patterns before production use.
